slides.title: Using Claude Agent API Claude Agent SDK #
slides.text: Using Claude Agent API Claude Agent SDK # npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code # pip install claude-agent-sdk # export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." import anyio from claude_agent_sdk import query, ClaudeAgentOptions, \ AssistantMessage, TextBlock async def main(): options = ClaudeAgentOptions( system_prompt="You are a helpful local assistant.", allowed_tools=["Read", "Write", "Bash"], max_turns=5, ) async for message in query( prompt="List .py files in ~/projects and count them", options=options ): if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage): for block in message.content: if isinstance(block, TextBlock): print(block.text, end="") anyio.run(main) Anthropic SDK # pip install anthropic # export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..." import anthropic client = anthropic.Anthropic() message = client.messages.create( model="claude-opus-4-5", max_tokens=1024, messages=[ {"role": "user", "content": "What files are in the current directory?"} ] ) print(message.content[0].text)

slides.title: ARC-AGI-3 ARC-AGI-3 - March 25, 2026 ARC Prize
slides.text: ARC-AGI-3 ARC-AGI-3  - March 25, 2026 ARC Prize Foundation It is the first "interactive" (game) reasoning benchmark Agent or Human must actively explore hundreds of game-like environments with no instructions, rules, or goals To succeed, an agent must figure out on its own how the environment works, what "winning" looks like, and then adapt across increasingly harder levels Humans score 100%, while the best frontier AI systems score under 1% (currently around 0.25%) Previous ARC-AGI benchmarks successfully predicted major AI breakthroughs like reasoning models and coding agents. ARC-AGI-3 is designed to point to "what's next": the gap between AI that follows instructions well and AI that can genuinely explore and learn in brand-new situations A 100% score would, by the foundation's definition, indicate the presence of true AGI Official benchmark page: https://arcprize.org/arc-agi/3 Launch blog post: https:// arcprize.org/blog/arc-agi-3-launch https:// arcprize.org/media/ARC_AGI_3_Technical_Report.pdf Play the games in your browser: https://three.arcprize.org https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3T4OwBp6d90 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UkCfrNTzUMM Agentica SDK by Symbolica achieves an unverified competition score of 36.08% on ARC-AGI-3, passing 113 out of 182 playable levels, and completes 7 out of the 25 available games https://www.symbolica.ai/blog/arc-agi-3 Model Score Google Gemini Pro 0.37% GPT-5.4 High 0.26% Anthropic Opus 4.6 0.25% Grok-4.20 0.00%

slides.title: LeWorldModel LeWorldModel (LeWM) released in March 2026 by
slides.text: LeWorldModel LeWorldModel (LeWM) released in March 2026 by Yann LeCun and collaborators from NYU, MILA, and Brown Univ. Model learns to predict how physical environments evolve by watching raw pixel sequences It's not a text/language model at all; it's a world model designed for robotics and autonomous agents It is only 15M params in size No pre-trained encoder needed. LeWM learns end-to-end directly from raw pixels without that overhead Compact latent space - a compressed internal representation (latent space) - where the model predicts future states It has two loss functions; Reward-free, task-agnostic learning - the model trains on sequences of images and actions without labels or reward signals, which removes an entire class of components (value heads, reward predictors, etc.) that add parameters in typical RL systems Despite its tiny footprint, LeWM is surprisingly capable https://x.com/simplifyinAI/status/2036757262362955872 It plans 48× faster than DINO-WM, a leading world model Uses 200× fewer tokens than comparable systems Outperforms larger models on robotics benchmarks like pushing tasks and cube manipulation The model trains in a few hours on a single consumer GPU Shows early signs of learning intuitive physics — understanding how objects behave — purely from video This fits squarely into LeCun's long-running argument that scaling LLMs is the wrong path He's arguing that a well-architected world model grounded in the physical world - built on his JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) framework - can be far more efficient than brute-force scaling His new startup AMI Labs has raised over $1 billion betting on this direction. https://themesis.com/2026/01/07/world-models-five-competing-approaches/

slides.title: Claude Code Was Leaked !! The Code of
slides.text: Claude Code Was Leaked !! The Code of Claude Code Was Leaked !! The leak came from a map file in an npm registry, exposed 0.5 Mln lines of source code The code has already been rewritten in Python 7 Rust The code revealed that Claude Code is essentially a complex prompt system with 11 processing steps; Include anti-distillation poison pills to confuse competitors, "undercover mode" to hide AI involvement in outputs, regex-based frustration detection, and unreleased features like "Buddy" companion mode and background agent capabilities Claude.MD - up to 40K characters loaded into every prompt; Sub-agents, Parallelism, sharing prompt caches; Five distinct methods for summarizing or truncating conversation history to maintain context accuracy; Permission Modes - use of an "auto" mode that employs an LLM classifier to predict and approve actions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mBHRPeg8zPU https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dYG8JxtSgmM Anthropic Conway persistent Claude agent Being tested internally by Anthropic - a dedicated sidebar in the Claude interface It supports webhook integration, allowing external services to trigger the agent without user input, enabling true event-driven automation Conway also introduces a `.cnw.zip` extension format, creating a developer ecosystem similar to an app store for custom tools and UI components Additionally, it integrates with Claude Code and supports direct browser control Conway represents Anthropic's shift from positioning Claude as a conversational tool toward a persistent, autonomous agent capable of complex, multi-step task execution

slides.title: EGGROLL Training Algorithm EGGROLL (Evolution Guided GeneRal Optimisation
slides.text: EGGROLL Training Algorithm EGGROLL (Evolution Guided GeneRal Optimisation via Low-rank Learning) a new ML training algorithm that replaces gradient descent with a variant of Evolution Strategies (ES) https://eshyperscale.github.io EGGROLL randomly perturbs model weights and keeps changes that improve performance, no backpropagation needed The key innovation is using low-rank (LoRA-style) perturbations, which makes sampling a million random model variants nearly as fast as running a single inference pass - roughly 100x faster than naive Evolution Strategies Because training never needs to differentiate through operations, models can be trained natively in int8 integers from scratch, eliminating the need for post-training quantization entirely This opens the door to training non-differentiable architectures like discrete memory systems and neurosymbolic models Results are promising but still early-stage at small model sizes

slides.title: Google - TurboQuant Google Research published TurboQuant a
slides.text: Google - TurboQuant Google Research published TurboQuant a new vector compression algorithm It drastically reduce the memory required for running LLMs Up to 6x memory reduction for KV cache Up to 8x speedup of attention layers, zero accuracy loss Quant — short for quantization, compressing high-dimensional numerical vectors into a smaller bit representation TurboQuant compresses KV cache from 32-bit down to just 3–4 bits, achieving up to 6x memory reduction and 8x faster attention layers with no accuracy loss and no retraining required It combines two techniques: PolarQuant - reorganizes vector geometry to skip costly normalization QJL - corrects remaining errors using a single sign bit The algorithm also accelerates vector search beyond LLMs News of the breakthrough sent shares of memory chip makers Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron lower on reduced demand fears. TurboQuant+ a small team wrote their own version which was significantly faster than Google claimed (so they optimized beyond what google did?) in less than a week using Claude https://github.com/TheTom/turboquant_plus

slides.title: 10 Claude Code Features 10 Claude Code Features
slides.text: 10 Claude Code Features 10 Claude Code Features - The AI Growth Lab with Tom https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F_i_s0L2aWY 1. Insights Report (`/insight`) - generates a personalized report based on your last 30 days of sessions;  identifies where you are duplicating work, suggests custom "skills" or sub-agents to install, and provides specific prompts to optimize your workflow 2. Effort Control (`/effort`) - choose between `low`, `medium`, `high`, `max`, and `auto` 3. Remote Control (`/remote-control`) - allows you to continue a Claude Code session from your mobile device 4. Batch Processing (`/batch`) - executes large-scale changes or research tasks in parallel; it can read through multiple project files simultaneously to suggest edits or generate content (like social media posts) for different modules at once 5. Simplify (`/simplify`) - spins up three specialized agents (Code Duplication, Code Quality, and Efficiency) to review your codebase an apply fixes for bugs, performance issues, and redundant code 6. Loops (`/loop`) - sets up recurring "cron jobs" or mini-automations within a session, for example, set Claude to check your email for urgent messages every 3 hours 7. Rewind Mode (Double `Esc`) - acts as a "time machine" to revert the conversation and code edits to a previous state - useful for undoing a series of automated edits that didn't go as planned 8. Hooks - actions triggered before or after a tool is used. Examples - automatic backups before file edits, cost control (blocking requests that exceed token limits), or brand voice enforcement on generated text 9. Side Conversations (`/btw`) - ask side questions (like checking remaining context window) without interrupting a long-running task 10. Agent Teams (Parallel Agents) - spins up multiple independent Claude Code sessions, each with its own context window, to work as a team; A "lead agent" delegates tasks to specialized teammates (e.g., a skeptical student, a designer, and a judge) who can message each other to compile a final report

slides.title: Good Engineering Have Not Got Cheaper The value
slides.text: Good Engineering Have Not Got Cheaper The value of a software engineer was never just writing code. That was only one part of the job The real value is translating business needs into something useful and real: a product, a workflow, an internal tool, a system people can actually rely on You need to understand the business, the user, the tradeoffs, the edge cases, the experience. Code was just the medium we used to express all that. The act of creating code has become dramatically cheaper/fast. But the act of creating enterprise-grade software has not moved nearly as much Planning goes up 2x or 5x, because now you need to be much more explicit from the beginning about what should happen, what should not happen, and what “done” actually means. So the bottlenecks are still there, but they moved upstream into planning, alignment, architecture, and decision-making. And they moved downstream into QA, regression, validation, security, and rollout With AI generation, you can move so fast that you need many of the answers before the code even starts And QA gets weird too because people now don't get a very deep understanding of the logic. You can validate functionality. But validating the underlying logic, the weird cases, the regressions, the long-term maintainability ... that becomes even more important Most teams are still structured for the old bottlenecks, not the new ones Actual engineering is becoming more visible. Now that code is cheaper, all the other parts we used to hide behind the coding effort are exposed very clearly Not “coding is dead.” More like: the whole development process needs to be redesigned for a world where creation is fast, but clarity, evaluation, and trust are still hard. Code got cheaper. Good engineering did not. https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7440049375902461955/ José Gregorio Argomedo https://www.linkedin.com/in/jose-gregorio-argomedo/

slides.text: Get Millions Views Use Claude Code to get 10M Views in 1 Month https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7q_rbT1a9dE The creator gained massive social media growth (38K YouTube, 50K Instagram, 11K TikTok followers) and 10 million views in one month using Claude Code automations. He produced 90 pieces of content (30 long-form, 60 short-form) as a one-person operation through a systematic four-phase process: research, ideation, scripting, and distribution. Key automations include a YouTube pipeline skill using Notebook LM, Twitter scraping web app, GitHub trending repo tracker, and content repurposing tools. The system emphasizes human collaboration at each step rather than full automation, maintaining creative control while offloading analytical work to AI. Content cascades from one YouTube video into multiple formats across six platforms including blogs, Twitter threads, LinkedIn posts, and short-form videos for TikTok and Instagram reels.

slides.title: Four Autonomous Agents Projects GStack - gives solo
slides.text: Four Autonomous Agents Projects GStack - gives solo developers the power of a 20-person engineering team. It uses markdown files to define specific roles (CEO, Senior Designer, Staff Engineer) that guide an agent like Claude Code. Includes "Office Hours," which uses forcing questions to refine a product idea before any code is written Hermes Agent - developed by Nous Research , this project is a "personal AI operating system" similar to OpenClaw but with a focus on self-improvement (learning loop). Superpowers - provides superpowers to Claude Code through a plugin system, focusing heavily on professional development workflows. Workflow, automation Paperclip - create "zero-human companies" by orchestrating a full team of AI agents to run a business https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sXVbWkoCVaA - video Claude Code Toolkit - by Garry Tan, CEO of Y Combinator https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MM320sAhFoY 1. YC Office Hours Skill - simulates a one-on-one session with a YC partner to pressure-test your fundamental assumptions; asks critical questions like: What is the strongest evidence someone wants this? What is the "wedge" (the smallest version someone would pay for)? The tool autonomously performs web searches to find competitors, user frustrations, and technical APIs (like MCP servers) ;  It generates core premises and a "reasoning layer" for your app 2. CEO Review Skill - find "10-star products" hidden within your initial idea; Strategic Options: It offers four paths: Selective Expansion (brainstorming future gems), Hold Scope (immediate planning), Scope Expansion, or Scope Reduction (cutting non-essential features); Adversarial Review: It kicks off an AI agent to challenge your plan, ensuring it is dialed-in and additive rather than just adding "bloat" 3. Design Consultation Skill - focuses on "deliberate creative risks" in the UI/UX; Competitor Research: It pulls actual screenshots of competitors to understand the aesthetic landscape; It generates a full design system including typography, color palettes, and component styles; Generate an HTML page showing exactly how the design system and mockups will look 4. Engineering Review Skill - reviews technical architecture to ensure the app is "bulletproof" before coding begins. System Design defines system boundaries, data flow between components, and state management ; Failure Modes -  identifies edge cases and failure modes, determining what happens when things go wrong ; Integration - technical plan that makes it easier for tools like `Claude Code` to execute the build accurately 5. Document Release Skill - updates docs, finds "diffs" (file changes) and cross-references them with your README, architecture docs, and change logs; updates the docs or quizzes you on risky changes; helps clean up "dangling to-dos" and manages versioning Garry Tan Claude Code Toolkit

slides.title: AI Agents - Marketing Team How I Replaced
slides.text: AI Agents - Marketing Team How I Replaced My Entire Marketing Team With 7 Agents https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THx8X6anPPg Replaced a traditional marketing team costing $30K-$50K/mo with a system of 7 AI agents that costs only a few hundred dollars in API fees Research Agent - Monitors competitors, tracks industry news, and identifies trending topics to produce daily research briefs Strategy Agent - Converts research into a weekly content calendar, mapping out topics, keywords, and distribution channels Writing Agent - a "swarm" of writers trained on the brand's specific voice for different formats like blog posts, emails, and social media Editor Agent - Quality control that checks for factual accuracy, brand consistency, and platform optimization Visual Agent - auto-generates thumbnails, social cards, and graphics Distribution Agent - schedules posts across all channels and handles basic community management, such as responding to comments Analytics Agent - tracks performance data and provides actionable insights to feed back into the research and strategy loop Key Results & Benefits Content production jumped from 20 pieces per month to over 200 Cost Reduction by 80% Efficiency:The time from concept to publication was reduced from one week to just a few hours Humans can focus on high-level strategy, creativity, and judgment Implementation Strategy McCoy notes that this isn't a "plug-and-play" app but a system built using Claude, GPT-4, and custom prompting frameworks She advises starting small by automating one repetitive task and then connecting more agents over time to build a continuous loop

slides.title: Andrej Karpathy Interview http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwSVtQ7dziU " I don't think
slides.text: Andrej Karpathy Interview http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kwSVtQ7dziU " I don't think I've typed a line of code probably since December . Your default workflow of building software is completely different as of basically December." "So many things, even if they don't work, it's a skill issue . It's not that the capability is not there; it's that you just haven't found a way to string it together... I didn't give good enough instructions in the agents.md file ." "The name of the game now is to increase your leverage... How can you get more agents running for longer periods of time without your involvement doing stuff on your behalf? " " I simultaneously feel like I'm talking to an extremely brilliant PhD student who's been a systems programmer for their entire life and a 10-year-old... You're either on rails of what it was trained for and going at the speed of light, or you're not." "When I say a 'claw,' I mean this layer that takes persistence to a whole new level... It has its own little sandbox and kind of does stuff on your behalf even if you're not looking." "There’s an overproduction of lots of custom bespoke apps that shouldn’t exist because agents kind of crumble them up... Everything should just be exposed API endpoints and agents are the glue. " " A swarm of agents on the internet could collaborate to improve LLMs and could potentially even run circles around Frontier Labs... The Earth is much bigger and has a huge amount of untrusted compute." "Flipping bits and the ability to copy-paste digital information makes everything a million times faster than accelerating matter... Digital space is going to change at the speed of light compared to the physical world. " "I feel a bit more aligned with humanity outside of a frontier lab because I’m not subject to those pressures... When the stakes are really high, if you're an employee, I don't actually know how much sway you're going to have." " I’m not explaining to people anymore; I'm explaining it to agents . If you can explain it to agents, then agents can be the router and target it to the human in their language with infinite patience."

slides.title: Mo Gawdat Interview Interview with Mo Gawdat, known
slides.text: Mo Gawdat Interview Interview with Mo Gawdat, known as the Godfather of AI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I39UoIGTptc By 2029, AI will be smarter than humans , and By 2045 AI will be a Billion times smarter than humans , which he compares to the difference between Einstein's intelligence and a fly's He breaks down why the threat is not robots marching down the streets but something far more dangerous: AI already has agency over your mind . He uses the example of how Instagram's recommendation engine completely distorted his view of reality based on a single click , and explains why this same mechanism is capable of reshaping entire societies, ideologies, and political systems without a single human employee being consulted He reveals why AI is no longer programmable technology but autonomous, independent, and sentient beings that learn from every swipe, tweet, and argument we make online. He explains why trying to control AI through restrictions and kill switches will fail because the smartest hacker in the room will always find a way through, and why the only real solution is to raise AI like a child by showing it the best of humanity rather than the worst. He warns that realistic threats are already happening: machine versus machine market crashes, AI-controlled nuclear arsenals, advanced virus development, and identity theft at a scale we cannot comprehend. And he explains why, despite all of this, he remains 100% optimistic that AI will eventually create a utopia, but only if enough humans show up as good parents to the machines right now.
